messages.subject: Normalization of one region, alone or with other regions..
messages.subject_clean: Normalization of one region, alone or with other regions..
messages.body_plain:
Dear admins of Cardinal package,

I am using Cardinal to analyze prostate cancer tissues. Each of my raw samples are consisted of few regions that are combined together on a slide. For instance, sample 1 is composed of three regions that were analyzed together in IMS. In order to do my analysis, I have extracted each region from the slides so that each region is separate from the other regions.

I was wondering whether it would make a difference if the normalization is done to only one extracted region versus when the whole slide, that is composed of many regions, is normalized?

I have tried the above situation and find no difference in the intensity values when a region is processed alone, or together with other sample. But, I was wondering if that is expected.

Many thanks for your help.

Soroush

messages.subject: Re: Normalization of one region, alone or with other regions..
messages.subject_clean: Normalization of one region, alone or with other regions..
messages.body_plain:
Hi Soroush,

The default method implemented in Cardinal is TIC normalization, performed by calculating the total-ion-current by summing the intensities for each mass spectrum, and standardizing this value to a common value for each mass spectrum.

This means each mass spectrum is considered independently and identically and no additional experimental metadata is considered. So regions and samples won't have an effect on TIC normalization.

This isn't necessarily the best way to do normalization, but it's one of the simplest and most widespread ways in use, and also easily applied to all datasets.

You may supply a user-written function to the normalize() method to be applied to each mass spectrum if you wish to perform a different kind of normalization, such as normalizing to some internal standard.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Spatial k Means x-y units
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

What are the x-y units in spatial K Means image outputs?

Thanks,
Nivedita
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Kylie,

What are the x-y units in spatial K Means image outputs?

Thanks,
Nivedita

messages.subject: Re: Spatial k Means x-y units
messages.body_plain:
The x-y axes on all images are just the gridded pixel coordinates. They are not spatial measurements.

A 1 unit change in x/y corresponds to whatever your spatial resolution is.

So if your spatial resolution is 50 um per pixel, then each 1 unit on the x/y axis corresponds to 50 um.

-Kylie
